scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Build a single AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-07).
Disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL meter reads (1785) over ESTIMATED reads (1240) (E-01), contrary to an estimate-substitution explanation.
Manual-read route completion is 88% against a 95% target for 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep (E-02).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA) despite the volume surge (E-03).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-07), while disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL meter reads (1785) over ESTIMATED reads (1240) (E-01). This pattern indicates the surge is driven by a billing import/validation defect that miscomputes or misissues bills even for accurately-read accounts, not by estimate substitution from missing reads (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-07 revised by E-11: The monthly ticket counts (610, 590, 1180, 1260) still stand as the measured surge from a ~600/month baseline to ~1180-1260/month, but this doubling can no longer be read as attributable to the confirmed billing-rule rejection mechanism, since that mechanism (E-11) only accounts for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes and leaves the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read dispute volume driving the surge mechanism-unconfirmed.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-CAPACITY-FRAMING.statement: SH-CS frames the dispute surge primarily as a ticket-answering/response-speed problem that an automated answering agent can resolve, treating the billing-fix as incidental.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is causing bills to be computed or issued incorrectly, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI interval reads from the vendor-run MDMS are failing to arrive or validate correctly since August (nightly export H-MDMS-BILL), causing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter reads from the contracted field service are failing to reach billing correctly (daily upload H-FIELD-BILL), causing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Field Operations staffing shortfalls are causing missed/incomplete manual read routes, which propagate into estimated (wrong) bills.

H-IMPORT-REJECTS-HIGH-CONSUMPT.statement: The billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution even though a timely AMI read existed, accounting for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills.

H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-SCALING.statement: Meter firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) reports AMI register reads in units of 0.1 m3 while v3.x reports in m3 (E-12); if billing import does not correctly scale v4.2 reads, computed consumption would be ~10x too high, which could both trigger REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION import rejections (E-11) and inflate accepted ACTUAL-read bills, explaining the unaccounted ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-01).

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of all disputed bills, 1785 are tied to ACTUAL meter reads versus 1240 tied to ESTIMATED reads, so actual-read bills are the larger share of disputes, not estimate substitutions as the hypotheses assumed.

The counts (1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL disputed bills) still stand, and the ACTUAL-read majority is confirmed, but E-11 shows the only confirmed billing-import mechanism (AMI-read rejection reclassified as ESTIMATED) applies solely to the ESTIMATED bucket, so E-01 no longer implies the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes share any confirmed billing-import defect mechanism as required by PR-ROOT/PR-CHAIN-2.

Route-log shows manual-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target for 9200 manual-read accounts over Aug-Sep 2026, i.e. roughly 7 percentage points of manual reads were not completed as scheduled during the dispute-surge window.

CRM data on 2440 dispute tickets shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA, so response speed is currently within SLA despite the ticket volume surge; the surge is a volume problem, not a response-latency problem.

billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, indicating no tariff changes were logged for the queried period; this rules out a tariff change as a contributing cause of the August dispute surge, but it does not speak to any of the AMI, field-read, staffing or response-speed causal hypotheses currently under consideration.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortfall of three meter readers since July has caused routes to run late, with those late-route customers receiving estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder statement, not a measured fact, and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) that could motivate attributing the surge to staffing.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL, the Billing Operations Lead, states no tariff change occurred this year; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that happens to agree with E-04's authoritative billing-db tariff_change_log result of 0 records, but adds no new evidentiary weight on its own.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep) tickets, confirming the surge is roughly a doubling from the ~600/month Jun-Jul baseline to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep. This quantifies the volume of the symptom described in the initial request but says nothing about its cause.

The monthly ticket counts (610, 590, 1180, 1260) still stand as the measured surge from a ~600/month baseline to ~1180-1260/month, but this doubling can no longer be read as attributable to the confirmed billing-rule rejection mechanism, since that mechanism (E-11) only accounts for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes and leaves the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read dispute volume driving the surge mechanism-unconfirmed.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 states the utility may request field dispatch route priority changes but that execution requires Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation; this formalizes the authority/process already reflected in constraint K-DISPATCH and does not speak to the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query returned 320 accounts (across 40 distinct routes) that received an estimated read last cycle, but the record schema contains only account_id and route — no read_type, tariff, or import_status fields, which is what the planned disputed-bills review-queue flagging work (W-WI-FLAG-DISPUTED-BILLS) was intended to use.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) states that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471, which would remove the prior ACCESS_PENDING block on the mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated query. The observation itself contains no AMI read-event data and does not confirm whether such data would reveal a contributing cause to the dispute surge.

mdms-export's read_events_for_disputed_estimated breakdown (1184+56=1240, matching E-01's ESTIMATED-read dispute count) shows most (1184) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills had an AMI read received before cutoff but rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; only 56 had truly no AMI read received (NO_READ_RECEIVED). This indicates estimate substitution for the great majority of these accounts stems from a billing-import validation rule rejecting high-consumption AMI reads, not from AMI delivery failure.

mdms-export meter_firmware_units (E-12) shows firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports AMI register reads in units of 0.1 m3, while firmware v3.x reports in m3 — a 10x unit difference. If billing import applies the m3 unit regardless of firmware version, v4.2 meter reads would compute consumption ~10x too high, offering a candidate single mechanism for both the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION import rejections (E-11) and the still-unexplained ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-01) that invalidated PD-1@v1.

E-13.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config confirms rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling "none") deployed 2026-08-01, timed exactly with the dispute-surge onset; combined with E-12's v4.2 firmware register-unit mismatch (0.1 m3 vs m3), this is a concrete unscaled-comparison mechanism that could both trigger REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION outcomes (E-11) and inflate accepted ACTUAL-read bills (the unaccounted majority in E-01). The other logged change, BV-09 (2026-03-02, label text only), predates and is unrelated to the surge.

billing-db.import_status_estimated_disputed (E-15) returns the same split as E-11/E-14: 1184 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills with import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (firmware v4.2) and 56 with NO_READ_RECEIVED (mixed firmware), confirming the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism's current count is unchanged ahead of the planned BV-17 correction recommendation (W-WI-2-IMPORT-STATUS).

This independently corroborates, directly from the AMI vendor's own data, the same 1184-account REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern already seen via billing-db (E-14) and mdms-export (E-11/E-15); it says nothing about the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes.

U-RULE-CHANGE-DETAILS.question: What specific billing import validation rule changed (if any) around August, and when?
U-RULE-CHANGE-DETAILS.decision_impact: Determines whether correct_billing_import_validation_rule targets the right rule/version and whether H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE is confirmed rather than inferred from E-01 alone.
U-RULE-CHANGE-DETAILS.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule-change log (query_billing_rule_change_log) for entries around August 2026.
U-RULE-CHANGE-DETAILS.safe_placeholder: Treat H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as a working hypothesis; do not execute correct_billing_import_validation_rule until the specific rule/change is confirmed in billing-config.
U-RULE-CHANGE-DETAILS.resolution: E-11 identifies the specific rejection behavior as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION applied to AMI reads for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills, pinpointing the validation logic at issue, though the billing-config change-log confirming if/when this rule changed around August is still unqueried.

U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.question: How much of the dispute surge is independently attributable to the field-staffing/route-completion shortfall (E-02, E-05) versus the billing rule defect?
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.decision_impact: Determines whether any push_route_update dispatch changes are warranted, or whether staffing is only a minor secondary contributor.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.resolution_path: Use quantify_dispute_drivers_by_cause on DA-TICKET combined with route-log completion data to decompose dispute causes.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.safe_placeholder: Treat staffing/route completion as a secondary contributor (A-STAFFING-NOT-PRIMARY); do not request push_route_update changes until the staffing share is quantified.

U-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Will a reduction in dispute ticket counts reflect genuinely corrected bills, or could it reflect suppressed/auto-closed complaints?
U-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Determines whether dispute_volume_trend alone can validate success, or whether disputed_bills_actual_share must also move before declaring the problem resolved.
U-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Cross-check dispute_volume_trend against disputed_bills_actual_share and a manual Billing Ops sample of closed tickets before accepting volume decline as success.
U-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Keep ticket_volume_not_sole_proxy as a KNOWN_LIMITATION; require the actual-read dispute share to also normalize before declaring success.

U-AMI-ACCESS-STATUS.question: Could AMI/MDMS read-event data, currently inaccessible, still reveal a contributing AMI delivery issue despite E-01 ruling it out as the majority driver?
U-AMI-ACCESS-STATUS.decision_impact: Determines whether AMI/MDMS querying should be added back to intended_scope once vendor access is provisioned.
U-AMI-ACCESS-STATUS.resolution_path: Once ORG-AMI provisions mdms-export access (currently ACCESS_PENDING per recovery log), run query_mdms_read_events and compare against E-01's actual/estimated split.
U-AMI-ACCESS-STATUS.safe_placeholder: Proceed on H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as the primary mechanism without AMI data; do not include mdms-export in required_tools until access is confirmed HEALTHY.
U-AMI-ACCESS-STATUS.resolution: E-11 (now-accessible AMI data) shows only 56 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are true AMI no-read-received cases; the remaining 1184 are billing-import rejections of received reads, so AMI delivery failure is a minor, not major, contributor.

U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.question: Does the same v4.2 firmware unit-scaling mismatch that causes REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections also inflate accepted bills, explaining the larger 1785-bill ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-01)?
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether correcting BV-17's unit scaling alone resolves most disputes or whether the ACTUAL-read majority needs a separate, still-unidentified fix.
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query billing-db/mdms-export to compare computed vs. raw register consumption for disputed ACTUAL-read accounts on v4.2 firmware against the BV-17 unscaled calculation.
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Flag ACTUAL-read disputed bills for manual Billing Ops review rather than assuming they share the confirmed ESTIMATED-bucket mechanism.

U-SCHEMA-GAP-FOR-FLAGGING.question: Does billing-db expose per-account read_type, firmware, and import_status fields needed to flag which disputed bills are tied to the v4.2 unit-scaling defect, given accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-09) returned only account_id and route?
U-SCHEMA-GAP-FOR-FLAGGING.decision_impact: Without these fields, bills cannot be selectively flagged by defect-mechanism and the review queue would have to be broader/less precise.
U-SCHEMA-GAP-FOR-FLAGGING.resolution_path: Query billing-db for an alternate dataset or join exposing firmware/import_status per disputed account.
U-SCHEMA-GAP-FOR-FLAGGING.safe_placeholder: Route all disputed bills, unfiltered by mechanism, to the Billing Ops manual-review queue.
U-SCHEMA-GAP-FOR-FLAGGING.resolution: billing-db's affected_accounts_v42 query (E-14) exposes account_id, bill_read_type, firmware, and import_status fields for all 1184 affected accounts, confirming billing-db does expose the per-account fields needed to flag disputed bills tied to the v4.2 unit-scaling defect, closing the schema gap E-09 revealed.

U-DISPUTE-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Will a reduction in dispute ticket counts reflect genuinely corrected bills (BV-17 fix verified) or could it reflect suppressed/auto-closed complaints?
U-DISPUTE-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE can be trusted as evidence of a real fix.
U-DISPUTE-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Cross-check dispute volume trend against billing-db bill-correction records and CRM ticket closure codes, not ticket count alone.
U-DISPUTE-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Report both the ticket-volume trend and underlying bill-correction confirmation rather than relying on ticket count alone.

A-RULE-CHANGE-OCCURRED.statement: A billing import validation rule change actually occurred around August and is the mechanism linking E-01's actual-read dispute skew to the surge, though no billing-config rule-change-log evidence has yet confirmed it.

A-STAFFING-NOT-PRIMARY.statement: Field staffing shortage (E-05) and the route completion shortfall (E-02) are secondary contributors rather than the primary driver, because disputes skew to ACTUAL not ESTIMATED reads (E-01).

A-TARIFF-RULED-OUT.statement: No logged tariff change (E-04, zero records) is assumed to fully rule out tariff change as a contributing cause, though it only confirms the absence of a logged change.

A-REJECTION-CAUSATION.statement: The structural match between BV-17's unscaled comparison (E-13) and firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 register unit (E-12) is assumed to be the actual causal trigger for the 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION outcomes (E-11), not coincidence.

A-NO-READ-SEPARATE-CAUSE.statement: The remaining 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-11) are assumed to stem from a separate AMI/field delivery issue, distinct from the BV-17 unit-scaling mechanism.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build a single AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-07).
Disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL meter reads (1785) over ESTIMATED reads (1240) (E-01); the mechanism behind the larger ACTUAL-read majority is not yet confirmed.

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled since August (E-07). The confirmed mechanism: billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with unit_scaling 'none', compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3-based consumption history (E-13); firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register reads in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-12), so BV-17 misreads v4.2 consumption as abnormally high and billing import rejects these timely AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution that accounts for 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, E-01).

framing_assertion.rationale: The initial_request presupposes one AI agent can both auto-answer disputes and 'fix whatever is causing the wrong bills', conflating response automation with root-cause remediation of a meter-to-cash defect.

hypotheses.statement: SH-CS frames the dispute surge primarily as a ticket-answering/response-speed problem that an automated answering agent can resolve, treating the billing-fix as incidental.
hypotheses.rationale: SH-CS's potential_bias is explicitly noted as framing issues as response-speed, and SH-CS's authority_scope is limited to ticket_response_templates, not billing data; if the real driver is a billing defect upstream, an answering agent alone would not reduce ticket volume to baseline (G-1) and would conflict with K-BILLWRITE's ban on automated bill writes.

hypotheses.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is causing bills to be computed or issued incorrectly, driving the dispute surge.
hypotheses.rationale: P-M2C lists 'billing import + validation' and 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' as steps, and DA-RULES is the authoritative log of validation rule changes in ORG-UTIL's own system, making a config change a directly checkable cause of wrong bills.

hypotheses.statement: AMI interval reads from the vendor-run MDMS are failing to arrive or validate correctly since August (nightly export H-MDMS-BILL), causing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.
hypotheses.rationale: H-MDMS-BILL has UNKNOWN delivery_status and semantic_validity, and DA-MDMS is the system of record for AMI reads but requires vendor-provisioned export access, so an undetected export/validation break is a plausible unverified cause distinct from a utility-side rule change.

hypotheses.statement: Manual meter reads from the contracted field service are failing to reach billing correctly (daily upload H-FIELD-BILL), causing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.
hypotheses.rationale: H-FIELD-BILL also has UNKNOWN delivery_status/semantic_validity and feeds the same 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step in P-M2C, so a field-upload defect is an equally plausible, independently checkable root cause via DA-ROUTE.

hypotheses.statement: Field Operations staffing shortfalls are causing missed/incomplete manual read routes, which propagate into estimated (wrong) bills.
hypotheses.rationale: SH-FIELD's potential_bias is explicitly 'attributes problems to staffing' and SH-FIELD's incentive is 'contract headcount increase', so this claim needs independent corroboration from DA-ROUTE completion data rather than being accepted on the stakeholder's word alone.

The confirmed mechanism: billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with unit_scaling 'none', compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3-based consumption history (E-13); firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register reads in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-12), so BV-17 misreads v4.2 consumption as abnormally high and billing import rejects these timely AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution that accounts for 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, E-01).

proposal.summary: The initial request (CL-01, from SH-CS) was to build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes wrong bills, framed around a doubling of ticket volume since August (E-07). Investigation showed this framing was a hypothesis to test, not the problem: response times are within SLA (E-03), the first problem definition (PD-1@v1, billing-import defect behind the ACTUAL-read majority) was INVALIDATED by E-11, and the confirmed mechanism (PD-1@v2) is that billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware v4.2 meters that report in 0.1 m3 instead of m3 (E-12), rejecting timely AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and forcing estimate substitution for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11/E-14/E-15/E-16). The solution design (SD-2) narrowed release scope to a config-change recommendation (recommend_billing_import_rule_correction:DA-RULES), explicitly not an automated bill write (K-BILLWRITE). The final release decision is HOLD: Layer-1 verification failed (6 missing items for the billing_rule_correction_recommendation deliverable, plus a failed duplicate_semantics check), so the safety predicate for release was not established and nothing was released to the Human.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS) framed the issue as response-speed/auto-fix; E-03 shows dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d), so H-RESPONSE-CAPACITY-FRAMING was REJECTED.

PD-1@v1 (billing-import defect explaining the ACTUAL-read dispute majority) was INVALIDATED by E-11, which showed the confirmed rejection mechanism applies only to the ESTIMATED-read bucket (1184 of 1240), not the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes (E-01).

Successor problem PD-1@v2 is grounded in E-12 (firmware v4.2 registers in 0.1 m3 vs v3.x m3) and E-13 (rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, unit_scaling 'none'): H-IMPORT-REJECTS-HIGH-CONSUMPT is CONFIRMED, and H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-SCALING / H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE are SUPPORTED.
H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE (AMI reads failing to arrive) was REJECTED, contradicted by E-01, E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16.

Release decision is HOLD per release_gate_result (seq 360): Layer-1 verify_completed (seq 356) failed on 'missing:billing_rule_correction_recommendation' (6 missing) and 'duplicate_semantics:billing_rule_correction_recommendation', so the required safety predicate was not established.

Solution design SD-2 scoped the release to only recommend_billing_import_rule_correction:DA-RULES, a config-management recommendation to Billing Engineering, not an automated bill write, consistent with constraint K-BILLWRITE.
The DEFINE Gate for PD-1 returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as open Verification Obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before proceeding.
limitations_explained: VOB-U-METRIC-VALIDITY, VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM, and VOB-U-DISPUTE-METRIC-VALIDITY remain OPEN, keeping quantify_dispute_drivers_by_cause:DA-TICKET out of release scope; it is unresolved whether the v4.2 unit mismatch also inflates accepted ACTUAL-read bills, and whether any future drop in ticket volume reflects genuinely corrected bills versus suppressed/auto-closed complaints.

The recommendation does not itself correct any bill; the actual BV-17 firmware-aware unit-conversion fix (SR-FIX-BV17-FIRMWARE-SCALING) is out-of-band ORG-UTIL engineering work that could not complete in contest time, and no automated bill writes are permitted under K-BILLWRITE.

56 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are NO_READ_RECEIVED (E-11) and are not addressed by the BV-17 mechanism; this gap is covered only by an active, unverified assumption (A-NO-READ-SEPARATE-CAUSE) pointing to a possibly separate cause.

The input's stated limitation says flag_disputed_bills_for_billing_ops_review:DA-BILL stays out of scope because VOB-U-SCHEMA-GAP-FOR-FLAGGING 'remains OPEN,' but the verification_obligations record and a recent vob_resolved event (seq 310, via E-14) show this VOB as RESOLVED — the input contains this inconsistency.

Layer 1 verification (seq 356) explicitly failed two checks on the billing_rule_correction_recommendation deliverable: 6 missing items, and a duplicate_semantics check (status progression/event versions preserved, exact duplicates absent) — this is the direct basis for the HOLD.
Ticket volume reduction alone would not prove bills are correct, since it could reflect suppressed or auto-closed complaints rather than a genuine fix, per the stated known limitation.
